normal-curve.def: A symmetric, bell-shaped frequency distribution in which most scores fall near the mean and fewer fall farther out; the mean, median and mode are equal.

empirical-rule.def: In a normal distribution, about 68% of scores lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two and 99.7% within three. Also called the empirical rule.

z-score.def: How many standard deviations a score is above (positive) or below (negative) the mean: $z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{\text{SD}}$. Also called a standard score.

percentile-rank.def: The percent of scores in a distribution that fall below a given score.
